content: Root cause: The bug was caused by the incorrect use of `u32` instead of `int` for checking negative error values returned by the `pm_runtime_get_sync()` function. This led to improper error handling, as negative values (indicating errors) were not being correctly identified, which could result in the system not properly managing the power runtime state. Additionally, there were issues in the error handling paths where the necessary cleanup actions (like calling `pm_runtime_put_sync()`) were not being performed when `pm_runtime_get_sync()` failed, potentially leading to resource leaks or incorrect reference counting.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect use of `u32` instead of `int` for checking negative error values returned by the `pm_runtime_get_sync()` function. This led to improper error handling, as negative values (indicating errors) were not being correctly identified, which could result in the system not properly managing the power runtime state. Additionally, there were issues in the error handling paths where the necessary cleanup actions (like calling `pm_runtime_put_sync()`) were not being performed when `pm_runtime_get_sync()` failed, potentially leading to resource leaks or incorrect reference counting.
Patch:
From d5afc1b68a6ddc27746d31f775025afe75ec8122 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tony Lindgren <tony@atomide.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Nov 2016 10:24:15 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] dmaengine: cppi41: More PM runtime fixes

Fix use of u32 instead of int for checking for negative errors values
as pointed out by Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>.

And while testing the PM runtime error path by randomly returning
failed values in runtime resume, I noticed two more places that need
fixing:

- If pm_runtime_get_sync() fails in probe, we still need to do
  pm_runtime_put_sync() to keep the use count happy. We could call
  pm_runtime_put_noidle() on the error path, but we're just going
  to call pm_runtime_disable() after that so pm_runtime_put_sync()
  will do what we want

- We should print an error if pm_runtime_get_sync() fails in
  cppi41_dma_alloc_chan_resources() so we know where it happens

Reported-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Fixes: 740b4be3f742 ("dmaengine: cpp41: Fix handling of error path")
Signed-off-by: Tony Lindgren <tony@atomide.com>
Signed-off-by: Vinod Koul <vinod.koul@intel.com>
---
 drivers/dma/cppi41.c | 11 +++++++----
 1 file changed, 7 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)

diff --git a/drivers/dma/cppi41.c b/drivers/dma/cppi41.c
index 4b52126c13cf..d5ba43a87a68 100644
--- a/drivers/dma/cppi41.c
+++ b/drivers/dma/cppi41.c
@@ -317,11 +317,12 @@ static irqreturn_t cppi41_irq(int irq, void *data)
 
 		while (val) {
 			u32 desc, len;
+			int error;
 
-			status = pm_runtime_get(cdd->ddev.dev);
-			if (status < 0)
+			error = pm_runtime_get(cdd->ddev.dev);
+			if (error < 0)
 				dev_err(cdd->ddev.dev, "%s pm runtime get: %i\n",
-					__func__, status);
+					__func__, error);
 
 			q_num = __fls(val);
 			val &= ~(1 << q_num);
@@ -367,6 +368,8 @@ static int cppi41_dma_alloc_chan_resources(struct dma_chan *chan)
 
 	error = pm_runtime_get_sync(cdd->ddev.dev);
 	if (error < 0) {
+		dev_err(cdd->ddev.dev, "%s pm runtime get: %i\n",
+			__func__, error);
 		pm_runtime_put_noidle(cdd->ddev.dev);
 
 		return error;
@@ -1072,8 +1075,8 @@ static int cppi41_dma_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
 	deinit_cppi41(dev, cdd);
 err_init_cppi:
 	pm_runtime_dont_use_autosuspend(dev);
-	pm_runtime_put_sync(dev);
 err_get_sync:
+	pm_runtime_put_sync(dev);
 	pm_runtime_disable(dev);
 	iounmap(cdd->usbss_mem);
 	iounmap(cdd->ctrl_mem);
--
